hardest_target_brief.title: Root Multiplicity Parity & Minimal Degree 5 Proof
hardest_target_brief.crux: Coordinate IVT sign trapping at x = 1 with constant-sign quadratic discriminant Delta < 0 to prove degrees 1-4 impossible, then construct explicit minimal degree 5 polynomial (1/12)(x-1)^2(x+1)(3x^2-10x+12).
hardest_target_brief.why_hardest: Demands coordinating three distinct advanced algebraic/topological theorems: (1) sign preservation across isolated zeros forcing even multiplicity >= 2; (2) irreducible quadratic sign constancy; (3) systematic degree-by-degree exhaustion with explicit specimen construction.

questions.X: Assuming tangency without sign crossing can occur at an odd multiplicity zero, or missing that degree <= 4 is saturated.
questions.Y: Demonstrated multiplicity parity theorem: odd multiplicity flips sign, even multiplicity preserves sign.
questions.Z: Zeros at +/-2 flip sign => mult >= 1; zero at 0 preserves negative sign => mult >= 2 (even). Total degree >= 1+1+2=4. Deg <= 4 forces mults 1, 1, 2 and fixes p(x) = x^2(x^2-4) = x^4 - 4x^2.
questions.W: Coordinate multiplicity inequalities to prove p(x) is uniquely x^4 - 4x^2.
